projects.title: bbhost
projects.status: Experimental; maintainer reports Bloodborne 1.09 playable, with PM4/compute work still hybrid.
projects.summary: Loads Bloodborne's original ELF, runs its x86-64 game code directly on the host CPU, binds PS4 imports to PC implementations, and uses SDL3/Vulkan/FFmpeg/ATRAC9 host services. Graphics are in transition: engine-level draws, post-processing and most shaders are native Vulkan/SPIR-V; compute dispatches and some commands still use a PM4 command processor. The project also rewrites selected game functions as source. Compatibility caveat: README says playable on Windows and Linux through world areas, bosses and online sessions. It lists known issues including some GPU hangs, shader/compute work still on the command processor, first-visit pipeline hitches, and summons that may need retrying. Performance varies considerably by GPU; compatibility is one title only.

projects.title: bbport
projects.status: Experimental playable; current renderer is shadPS4-derived PM4 processing; direct GNM-to-Vulkan translation is a stated next step.
projects.summary: Offline-converts the executable to a memory image, links selected PS4 libc/Fios2 code, and runs game CPU code natively with a title-specific runtime replacing only the system functions Bloodborne uses. Current renderer derives from shadPS4: it decodes PM4 command streams and recompiles GCN shaders for Vulkan. The maintainer describes direct GnmDriver-call-to-Vulkan and SPIR-V translation, without command-processor emulation, as the next graphics step, so it should not be described as already being a full DXVK-style API translator. Compatibility caveat: Maintainer calls it experimental but playable: boot, save/load, sound, gamepad and several areas were exercised; no full playthrough or broad hardware support has been verified. Thorough validation is reported on one Linux/RADV AMD RX 7800 XT and some Steam Deck testing; README warns of possible crashes and NVIDIA limitations in the experimental memory path.

projects.subtype: Game-specific console compatibility (PM4/GPU-emulation path; direct API translation planned)

projects.status: Experimental; title milestones are tracked, but gameplay/menu milestones do not imply full-game playability.
projects.summary: Loads and links PS5 modules into a host address space; reimplements Sony HLE libraries over host facilities; adapts guest ABI details; decodes AGC/PM4 commands and recompiles RDNA2 shaders to SPIR-V, then translates GPU state/draws to Vulkan. Compatibility caveat: As of the checked 2026-10-09 compatibility report: 54 tracked titles; 26 reached gameplay with a rendered scene, 17 reached a title/menu or gameplay without a rendered world, 3 reached only a logo/splash, and 8 booted without content frames. The author explicitly says these milestones do not imply complete-game playability; some results are route-dependent or visually degraded.

directory_items.name: decomp.me
directory_items.description: A browser-based collaborative workspace for matching individual functions with project-specific compiler presets.

directory_items.name: Proton
directory_items.description: Valve's Steam compatibility tool for running many Windows PC games on Linux, built around Wine and additional components.
directory_items.source_evidence: Valve's repository describes Proton's Windows-game-on-Linux purpose and documents its Wine basis and graphics components such as DXVK and vkd3d-proton.

directory_items.name: objdiff
directory_items.description: A local GUI for comparing rebuilt object files against target objects and inspecting function and data differences.
directory_items.source_evidence: The project README describes object-file comparison, automatic rebuilds, progress reporting, and support for several console CPU families.

directory_items.name: DXVK
directory_items.description: A Vulkan-based implementation of Direct3D 8, 9, 10, and 11 used with Wine and in compatibility stacks such as Proton.
directory_items.source_evidence: The project README states the Direct3D versions and Vulkan target, and explains use through Wine and Steam Play tools.

directory_items.name: vkd3d-proton
directory_items.description: A Proton-focused implementation of Direct3D 12 on Vulkan, complementary to DXVK's Direct3D 8–11 coverage.
directory_items.source_evidence: The upstream README describes the project as implementing Direct3D 12 on Vulkan and as the development effort behind Proton's D3D12 support.

directory_items.name: Floating IPS (Flips)
directory_items.description: A desktop and command-line patcher for creating and applying IPS and BPS patches, useful for distributing fan-made changes without bundling a game image.
directory_items.source_evidence: The maintainer README documents IPS/BPS creation and application, GUI and command-line use, and release downloads.

directory_items.name: Ghidra
directory_items.description: An extensible reverse-engineering suite with disassembly and decompilation features for inspecting compiled game code.
directory_items.source_evidence: The NSA-maintained project describes Ghidra as a software reverse-engineering framework and lists disassembly and decompilation among its capabilities.

directory_items.name: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
directory_items.description: An open-source MCP server and CLI that lets coding agents inspect websites, Electron applications, and native binaries with local analysis tools, returning findings with evidence and limitations.
directory_items.source_evidence: The project README describes REA as an agent-connected reverse-engineering tool for websites, applications, and native binaries; it says analysis runs locally and returns evidence and limitations. The repository is public, MIT-licensed, and has a release published 2026-10-14.

directory_items.name: N64: Recompiled
directory_items.description: A toolchain that statically recompiles N64 binaries into C for building native ports and related projects.
directory_items.source_evidence: The maintainer README describes the binary-to-C workflow and notes that symbol/build metadata is required; it is not a one-click port generator.

directory_items.name: GameBanana
directory_items.description: A cross-game community site for discovering and publishing mods, tools, and other game-specific submissions.
directory_items.source_evidence: GameBanana's community guide describes game-specific modding communities, submissions, and volunteer game managers; the live homepage showed active trending and recent community content.
